sessions.notes: Connect to research writing and academic presentations.
sessions.title: Nuanced Academic Discourse
sessions.objective: Use precise academic vocabulary to discuss research, theories, and methodologies with appropriate register.
sessions.context: Engaging in sophisticated academic discussions and research.

sessions.notes: Practice with authentic business scenarios; discuss overuse and clarity.
sessions.title: Idiomatic Business Language
sessions.objective: Navigate business idioms and corporate jargon appropriately in professional contexts.
sessions.context: Participating in corporate environments and strategic discussions.

sessions.notes: Use simplified contract excerpts; emphasize comprehension over production.
sessions.title: Legal and Contractual Language
sessions.objective: Recognize formal legal terminology and understand contractual language structure.
sessions.context: Understanding and discussing legal documents and agreements.

sessions.notes: Connect to well-being discussions and interpersonal relationships.
sessions.title: Psychological and Emotional Complexity
sessions.objective: Express subtle psychological concepts and emotional nuances accurately.
sessions.context: Discussing mental states, personality, and emotional intelligence.

sessions.notes: Use current events; maintain political neutrality.
sessions.title: Political and Governance Vocabulary
sessions.objective: Understand and use political terminology to discuss governance and policy.
sessions.context: Following and discussing political systems and international relations.

sessions.notes: Practice with diagrams and process descriptions.
sessions.title: Scientific and Technical Precision
sessions.objective: Use technical vocabulary accurately to describe scientific concepts and processes.
sessions.context: Explaining scientific processes and technical procedures.

sessions.notes: Compare different media sources and analyze framing.
sessions.title: Media and Journalistic Language
sessions.objective: Identify and discuss media language, bias, and reporting techniques.
sessions.context: Analyzing news media and journalistic writing.

sessions.notes: Connect to global issues and personal action.
sessions.title: Environmental and Sustainability Issues
sessions.objective: Express complex environmental concepts and discuss policy implications.
sessions.context: Discussing environmental challenges and solutions.

sessions.notes: Practice with authentic works; encourage personal interpretation.
sessions.title: Cultural and Artistic Criticism
sessions.objective: Use sophisticated vocabulary to critique and interpret cultural products.
sessions.context: Analyzing and discussing art, literature, and cultural works.

sessions.notes: Use graphs and current economic data.
sessions.title: Economic Theory and Finance
sessions.objective: Use economic terminology to discuss market trends and financial concepts.
sessions.context: Understanding and discussing economic principles and financial markets.

sessions.notes: Focus on patient perspective; avoid overly technical language.
sessions.title: Healthcare and Medical Terminology
sessions.objective: Understand medical vocabulary for patient-provider communication and health literacy.
sessions.context: Discussing healthcare, medical procedures, and patient care.

sessions.notes: Present ethical scenarios; encourage respectful debate.
sessions.title: Philosophical and Ethical Concepts
sessions.objective: Use philosophical vocabulary to examine ethical questions and moral reasoning.
sessions.context: Engaging in philosophical discussions and ethical debates.

sessions.notes: Keep updated with current tech trends.
sessions.title: Technology and Digital Innovation
sessions.objective: Use tech vocabulary to discuss innovation, implications, and societal impact.
sessions.context: Discussing technological advances and digital transformation.

sessions.notes: Role-play complex scenarios; focus on diplomatic language.
sessions.title: Interpersonal Dynamics and Conflict
sessions.objective: Express nuanced interpersonal situations and conflict resolution strategies.
sessions.context: Managing complex interpersonal relationships and conflicts.

sessions.notes: Use excerpts from various genres.
sessions.title: Literary Devices and Analysis
sessions.objective: Identify and discuss literary devices and narrative techniques.
sessions.context: Analyzing literature and creative writing techniques.

sessions.notes: Use images of buildings and city plans.
sessions.title: Architecture and Urban Planning
sessions.objective: Use architectural vocabulary to discuss design, planning, and urban issues.
sessions.context: Discussing built environments and city development.

sessions.notes: Connect to cultural identity and globalization.
sessions.title: Food Culture and Gastronomy
sessions.objective: Use sophisticated food vocabulary to describe tastes, techniques, and culture.
sessions.context: Discussing food traditions, cooking, and dining experiences.

sessions.notes: Emphasize multiple perspectives and historical thinking.
sessions.title: Historical Analysis and Historiography
sessions.objective: Use historical vocabulary to discuss events, causation, and historical interpretation.
sessions.context: Analyzing historical events and historical writing.

sessions.notes: Challenge: Highly abstract concepts. Use examples from multiple languages if possible.
sessions.title: Abstract Linguistic Concepts (Optional Harder)
sessions.objective: Understand and use metalinguistic vocabulary to analyze language itself.
sessions.context: Discussing language structure, meaning, and variation.

sessions.notes: Challenge: Politically sensitive topics. Maintain objectivity and present multiple viewpoints.
sessions.title: Geopolitics and International Relations (Optional Harder)
sessions.objective: Use advanced political vocabulary to discuss global power dynamics and international affairs.
sessions.context: Analyzing complex international political relationships and historical movements.

sessions.notes: Challenge: Highly abstract philosophical concepts. Use thought experiments and clear examples.
sessions.title: Epistemology and Theory of Knowledge (Optional Harder)
sessions.objective: Use philosophical terminology to discuss how we know what we know.
sessions.context: Examining philosophical questions about knowledge and belief.

sessions.notes: Practice with sentence combination and text improvement.
sessions.title: Advanced Participle Clauses
sessions.structure: Having + past participle; Being + past participle; participle clauses for cause, time, concession
sessions.objective: Use participle clauses to reduce redundancy and create cohesive, elegant sentences.
sessions.context: Creating concise, sophisticated written and spoken discourse.

sessions.notes: Contrast with British vs American usage.
sessions.title: Subjunctive Mood in Formal Contexts
sessions.structure: It is essential/vital/imperative that + subject + base verb; I suggest/demand that
sessions.objective: Recognize and produce subjunctive forms in formal written and spoken English.
sessions.context: Formal recommendations, requirements, and proposals.

sessions.notes: Balance nominalization with clarity; discuss when to avoid it.
sessions.title: Nominalization for Academic Writing
sessions.structure: Converting verbs/adjectives to nouns (discover → discovery, efficient → efficiency)
sessions.objective: Use nominalization to create dense, formal prose appropriate to academic contexts.
sessions.context: Formal academic and professional writing.

sessions.notes: Practice with text analysis and paraphrasing.
sessions.title: Ellipsis and Substitution
sessions.structure: Omitting repeated elements; using 'do so', 'one', 'the former/latter'
sessions.objective: Use ellipsis and substitution naturally to create cohesive, elegant text.
sessions.context: Avoiding repetition in sophisticated discourse.

sessions.notes: Analyze authentic speeches for emphasis techniques.
sessions.title: Fronting and Emphasizing Structures
sessions.structure: What I need is...; All I want is...; The thing that matters is...
sessions.objective: Use fronting structures to control information flow and emphasis.
sessions.context: Emphasizing information in speech and writing.

sessions.notes: Essential for academic writing; practice with claims and evidence.
sessions.title: Hedging and Boosting Language
sessions.structure: Modal expressions (may, might, could); intensifiers (certainly, clearly, undoubtedly)
sessions.objective: Use hedging to express caution and boosting to express certainty appropriately.
sessions.context: Academic writing and professional communication requiring precision about certainty.

sessions.notes: Practice with argumentative writing and debate.
sessions.title: Adverbial Clauses of Concession
sessions.structure: Although, even though, despite the fact that, while, whereas, much as
sessions.objective: Use various concessive structures to acknowledge counterarguments and complexity.
sessions.context: Presenting contrasting information in arguments and analysis.

sessions.notes: Practice with hypothetical past and present situations.
sessions.title: Conditionals: Mixed and Implied
sessions.structure: Otherwise, or else, but for, with, without + would/could have
sessions.objective: Express conditional meaning without explicit 'if' structures; use various conditional markers.
sessions.context: Expressing complex conditional relationships implicitly.

sessions.notes: Use timeline visuals; practice with planning scenarios.
sessions.title: Future Perfect and Future Continuous
sessions.structure: Will have + past participle; will be + -ing
sessions.objective: Use future perfect and continuous to express actions in progress or completed at future times.
sessions.context: Making predictions and discussing future situations with temporal precision.

sessions.notes: Analyze academic texts for cohesive devices.
sessions.title: Discourse Markers and Cohesion
sessions.structure: Furthermore, moreover, nevertheless, nonetheless, conversely, by contrast, to this end
sessions.objective: Use sophisticated discourse markers to signal relationships between ideas.
sessions.context: Creating logical flow in extended discourse.

sessions.notes: Distinguish between formal and informal passive forms.
sessions.title: Passive Voice: Advanced Forms
sessions.structure: Get-passive; need + -ing; be + supposed to; passive infinitives and gerunds
sessions.objective: Use full range of passive forms appropriately across contexts.
sessions.context: Varied passive constructions for different registers and purposes.

sessions.notes: Practice with complex sentence building.
sessions.title: Relative Clauses: Reduced and Complex
sessions.structure: Preposition + which/whom; reduced relative clauses; sentential relative clauses
sessions.objective: Use advanced relative clause structures for precision and sophistication.
sessions.context: Creating dense, information-rich noun phrases.

sessions.notes: Practice with academic citation and news reporting.
sessions.title: Reporting Verbs and Structures
sessions.structure: Suggest, recommend, insist, deny, claim + that/to/gerund; reporting with modals
sessions.objective: Use a wide range of reporting verbs with correct complementation patterns.
sessions.context: Accurately reporting speech and thought with nuanced meaning.

sessions.notes: Balance complexity with clarity; practice unpacking dense phrases.
sessions.title: Complex Noun Phrases
sessions.structure: Multiple modifiers; embedded clauses; of-phrases; apposition
sessions.objective: Build complex noun phrases with multiple layers of modification.
sessions.context: Academic and professional writing requiring information density.

sessions.notes: Distinguish between different causative meanings.
sessions.title: Causative Structures
sessions.structure: Have/get something done; make/let/have someone do; get someone to do
sessions.objective: Use causative verbs appropriately to express different levels of causation and agency.
sessions.context: Describing caused actions and permissions in various registers.

sessions.notes: Practice with reflection and alternative scenarios.
sessions.title: Unreal Past and Wish Structures
sessions.structure: I wish/if only + past perfect; it's time; would rather; as if/as though
sessions.objective: Use unreal past structures to express complex counterfactual meanings.
sessions.context: Expressing regret, preferences, and hypothetical situations.

sessions.notes: Practice with mystery scenarios and problem-solving.
sessions.title: Modal Perfects for Speculation
sessions.structure: Must/might/could/can't have + past participle
sessions.objective: Use modal perfect forms to express varying degrees of certainty about the past.
sessions.context: Making deductions and speculations about past events.

sessions.notes: Contrast with informal alternatives.
sessions.title: It-Structures and Extraposition
sessions.structure: It is adjective that...; It takes...; It occurs/happens that...
sessions.objective: Use it-structures for extraposition and creating formal tone.
sessions.context: Creating formal, impersonal constructions in academic writing.

sessions.notes: Challenge: Unusual word order. Use literary texts and formal speeches.
sessions.title: Inversion After Negative Adverbials (Optional Harder)
sessions.structure: Rarely/Seldom/Never/Hardly/Scarcely + auxiliary + subject + verb
sessions.objective: Recognize and produce inverted structures after negative adverbials for dramatic effect.
sessions.context: Creating emphasis in formal written and literary contexts.

sessions.notes: Challenge: Formal and somewhat archaic. Focus on recognition in reading.
sessions.title: Conditionals with Inversion (Optional Harder)
sessions.structure: Had I known...; Were it not for...; Should you need...
sessions.objective: Use inverted conditional forms without 'if' for formal register.
sessions.context: Formal writing and speech requiring sophisticated conditional expressions.

sessions.notes: Challenge: Agreement rules with correlatives. Practice with sentence combining.
sessions.title: Complex Coordination and Correlatives (Optional Harder)
sessions.structure: Not only...but also; neither...nor; both...and; either...or (with subject-verb agreement)
sessions.objective: Use correlative conjunctions correctly with proper parallelism and agreement.
sessions.context: Creating balanced, sophisticated compound structures.

sessions.notes: Teach signposting and transitional phrases; practice fielding challenging questions.
sessions.title: Academic Presentations with Q&A
sessions.objective: Delivering a formal academic presentation on research or complex topic with questions.
expressions: I'd like to draw your attention to...
Let me elaborate on that point...
sessions.functions: presenting; structuring; signposting; handling questions; defending positions

sessions.notes: Focus on diplomatic language and keeping discussions on track.
sessions.title: Chairing and Facilitating Meetings
sessions.objective: Leading a professional meeting with multiple stakeholders and competing interests.
expressions: Let's move to the next agenda item...
To summarize the discussion so far...
We need to reach a decision on...
Let's table this for now and...

sessions.notes: Emphasize tone and body language; practice hedging language.
sessions.title: Diplomatic Disagreement
sessions.objective: Disagreeing professionally while maintaining relationships and respect.
expressions: I'd like to offer an alternative view...
sessions.functions: disagreeing politely; acknowledging others; offering alternatives; softening criticism

sessions.notes: Teach attribution and synthesis; practice avoiding plagiarism.
sessions.title: Synthesizing Multiple Sources
sessions.objective: Presenting information from various sources with analysis and evaluation.
expressions: According to X, while Y argues...
When we consider X in light of Y...

sessions.notes: Emphasize curiosity over assumptions; discuss cultural intelligence.
sessions.title: Intercultural Communication
sessions.objective: Navigating cultural differences in professional and social contexts.
expressions: I want to make sure I'm understanding correctly...
sessions.functions: clarifying; checking understanding; adapting communication; showing respect; navigating norms

sessions.notes: Focus on clarity, calmness, and transparency under pressure.
sessions.title: Crisis Communication
sessions.objective: Communicating effectively during emergencies or organizational crises.
expressions: Here's what we know at this time...
We are taking the following steps...
sessions.functions: informing; reassuring; directing; updating; maintaining transparency

sessions.notes: Teach feedback frameworks (e.g., SBI model); balance positive and developmental.
sessions.title: Mentoring and Giving Feedback
sessions.objective: Providing constructive feedback and guidance to colleagues or mentees.
expressions: I've noticed that you excel at...
sessions.functions: evaluating; encouraging; advising; critiquing constructively; goal-setting

sessions.notes: Teach structuring techniques; practice with varied topics.
sessions.title: Impromptu Speaking
sessions.objective: Speaking without preparation on complex or abstract topics.
expressions: Let me think about that for a moment...
I would approach this from two angles...
Building on what was just said...
sessions.functions: organizing thoughts quickly; structuring spontaneously; buying time; concluding effectively

sessions.notes: Connect to written academic discourse; practice objective tone.
sessions.title: Academic Writing Discussions
sessions.objective: Discussing research, methodology, and findings in academic contexts.
sessions.functions: describing methodology; presenting findings; analyzing implications; acknowledging limitations

sessions.notes: Teach argumentation structure; practice rhetorical devices.
sessions.title: Persuasive Argumentation
sessions.objective: Building and presenting complex, persuasive arguments on controversial topics.
expressions: We cannot ignore the fact that...
sessions.functions: arguing; providing evidence; anticipating objections; countering; concluding powerfully

sessions.notes: Practice turn-taking and collaborative discourse.
sessions.title: Panel Discussions
sessions.objective: Participating in panel discussions with multiple experts and audience questions.
expressions: I'd like to add a different perspective...
I'm glad you raised that because...
sessions.functions: contributing; building on others' points; managing turns; engaging audience; responding to questions

sessions.notes: Emphasize clarity and audience awareness; use visuals.
sessions.title: Explaining Complex Processes
sessions.objective: Making complex technical or conceptual processes clear to non-experts.
sessions.functions: simplifying; analogizing; sequencing; checking understanding; visualizing

sessions.notes: Balance professional and personal; practice authenticity.
sessions.title: Networking and Professional Relationships
sessions.objective: Building and maintaining professional relationships through conversation.
expressions: I'd love to hear more about...
Is there any way I can help with...?
I was thinking about our conversation...
sessions.functions: small talk; showing interest; following up; offering help; staying in touch

sessions.notes: Emphasize cultural sensitivity and empathy.
sessions.title: Handling Sensitive Topics
sessions.objective: Discussing difficult or sensitive subjects with tact and respect.
expressions: This is a sensitive topic, but...
I hope you don't mind my asking...
I understand this must be difficult...
Please let me know if you'd rather not discuss...
sessions.functions: approaching carefully; showing sensitivity; using euphemisms; respecting boundaries; supporting

sessions.notes: Practice message discipline and bridging techniques.
sessions.title: Media Interviews
sessions.objective: Being interviewed by media and staying on message under pressure.
expressions: What we're really talking about is...
I'd like to come back to...
sessions.functions: staying on message; bridging; managing difficult questions; sound bites; clarity

sessions.notes: Focus on persuasive language and call to action.
sessions.title: Policy and Advocacy
sessions.objective: Advocating for policy changes or organizational reforms.
sessions.functions: proposing; justifying; addressing concerns; mobilizing support; maintaining momentum

sessions.notes: Challenge: High cognitive load. Start with short passages; build up gradually.
sessions.title: Simultaneous Interpretation Practice (Optional Harder)
sessions.objective: Practicing basic consecutive interpretation between English and learners' L1.
expressions: Let me make sure I understood...
sessions.functions: listening actively; note-taking; reproducing message; managing cognitive load

sessions.notes: Challenge: Requires philosophical thinking and patience. Model respectful questioning.
sessions.title: Socratic Dialogue and Critical Inquiry (Optional Harder)
sessions.objective: Engaging in Socratic method questioning to explore ideas deeply.
expressions: What would be an example of...?
sessions.functions: questioning assumptions; probing; challenging; clarifying; seeking consistency

sessions.notes: Challenge: Meta-level analysis of language. Use political speeches and advertisements.
sessions.title: Rhetorical Analysis and Deconstruction (Optional Harder)
sessions.objective: Analyzing and deconstructing persuasive texts for rhetorical strategies.
sessions.functions: identifying rhetoric; analyzing effectiveness; critiquing; recognizing manipulation
